title: Unbounded Speculative Hedged Requests
damaged_code:
```rust
let futures = replicas.iter().map(|node| node.read(key));
let first_response = select_all(futures).await; // Redundant calls sent unconditionally
```
pattern: Automatically or unconditionally issuing speculative duplicate/hedged requests to multiple replicas to reduce tail latency, without capping the rate of hedged requests or client-side load.
why_bad: Hedged requests are helpful under normal loads. However, if a backend is struggling due to high load or network congestion, unconditionally duplicating requests doubles or triples the traffic. This completely saturates the remaining capacity of the cluster, transforming a minor slowdown into a catastrophic denial-of-service [30, 140].
detection: Detect redundant/speculative requests sent in parallel to multiple replicas where there is no throttling, rate-limiting, or conditional limit on the fraction of requests that can be speculatively duplicated.
counterexample: Configure a system where a hedged request is only sent if the primary request takes longer than the 95th percentile expected latency (e.g. 200ms), and cap the total number of hedged requests at 5% of overall client traffic.
fix: Implement hedging thresholds (only send duplicate requests if the primary call exceeds a high-percentile duration) and strictly limit the total percentage of hedged requests to protect backend capacity.
source: Alex Petrov, *Database Internals*, page 238 / passage [30] or Titus Winters et al., *Software Engineering at Google*, page 527 / passage [140].
